subject: Post-call: Account health, new workloads & scale path for Courier Analytics
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Renee Caldwell <renee@courieranalytics.com>, Kunal Mehta <kunal@courieranalytics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Account health, new workloads & scale path for Courier Analytics

Hi Renee / Kunal —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our conversation and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. I captured the bits we discussed and annotated a recommended expansion path.

Top pain points you confirmed:
- Search relevance degradation as dataset grows (current embedding infra saturating at peak loads).
- Rising per-token costs from naïve batching and long generation paths.
- Need for stronger operational visibility (route-level latency SLOs + alerting).

Goals you shared:
- Reduce average search latency to <120ms P95 for user-facing queries.
- Cut inference unit cost by ~28% while maintaining top-3 result quality.
- Run a controlled pilot moving RAG and embeddings to a Dedicated pool for 90 days.

What we propose (high level):
1) 90-day Dedicated pilot (2x A100-equivalent capacity) focused on embeddings + RAG traffic for the northern-hemisphere peak window.
2) Move cold/low-priority generation to a cheaper quantized variant with prefix caching; preserve top-tier model for interactive low-latency queries.
3) Instrument model + route dashboards in Redwood Console; set regression alerting against your prompt set.

Attachments: usage_snapshot_apr2027.csv (token distribution + peak windows), pilot-scope-appendix.pdf. I will draft a mutual action plan and include a suggested timeline and success metrics.

Immediate next steps:
- I’ll share a MAP and pilot quote by EOD tomorrow.
- Dylan to follow up with a technical appendix and sizing notes.
- Renee / Kunal: confirm internal PO timeline and any procurement constraints (DocuSign or PO process).

Proposed timeline:
- Week 1: finalize MAP + PO sign-off
- Week 2–3: provisioning & QA in your VPC (if required) / onboarding
- Week 4–12: pilot execution, weekly check-ins, success review at day 60 and 90

Thanks — happy to adjust.

—
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189

From: Renee Caldwell <renee@courieranalytics.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kunal Mehta <kunal@courieranalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 17:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Account health, new workloads & scale path for Courier Analytics

Thanks Ava — solid recap, appreciate the level of detail. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement & PO: We typically require a signed SOW + invoice to process a PO. Targeting end of month for approval but I need to confirm with finance tomorrow.
2) Data residency / controls: For the pilot we need to ensure logs are retained within US regions and that you can turn on strict audit logging (SOC2-ready).
3) Pilot scope: Confirm whether the pilot can be limited to a single product line (ShipSync only) so we can isolate metrics.

We’d like the MAP and rough cost estimate to share internally. Also loop in your CS lead if possible — they’ll want to validate success metrics.

Kunal — tagging you for procurement timeline visibility.

Renee
Head of Product, Courier Analytics
renee@courieranalytics.com

Renee / Kunal —

Short technical follow-up from my side based on your data residency and pilot-scope asks:

- Residency / audit logging: We can provision the Dedicated pilot in the US-east region and enable audit logs to your KMS. Redwood Private also supports customer-managed HSM if you need keys in a particular HSM vendor. I’ll add the SOC2 evidence pack to the MAP.

- Pilot scope / isolation: Absolutely — we recommend starting with ShipSync only. That keeps traffic focused and simplifies success metrics (search latency, recall@5, cost/unit).

- Sizing suggestion: Based on the usage CSV, target peak concurrent tokens and an assumed 30% cache hit; I recommend a 2-node Dedicated pool (A100-eq) with autoscale floor set to 1 and burst to 3 for weekend loads. I attached a short appendix with exact CPU/GPU estimates and an example batching config.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_Courier_Analytics.docx (draft MAP), pilot-scope-appendix.pdf

If useful, I can run a short synthetic load test against a sandbox model next week to validate latency tail behavior. What days work for you?

—
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
